title: COVER-Fish pointer audit v2 scientific and execution artifact catalog
description: Structural catalog for frozen v0.2 serial receipts and additive v0.3 process receipts. TSV record schemas describe decoded row objects; orderedHeaders are the exact physical TSV headers.
transactionRules: pointer-health-attempts.tsv is append-only
a completion commits one logically contiguous attempt-index range for one record, window, and invocation; global file adjacency and global timestamp order are not scientific invariants
a disposition and completion are mutually exclusive for an attempt
window_id and invocation_id are one-to-one and a window_id is never reused
v0.2 fsync-appends each evaluated attempt to the canonical ledger before the next request
v0.3 fsync-appends evaluated receipt rows to a private per-record spool; the coordinator alone canonicalizes robots, attempts, then completion before worker-slot reuse
v0.3 physical canonical order follows worker-completion events while deterministic IDs and record-local attempt indexes define logical order
v0.3 completed spools are canonicalized and durable incomplete attempts are dispositioned before resume; a terminal receipt has no .parallel-work-v03 tree

v0.3 workers hold a shared stable-inode lease for their full process lifetime; recovery obtains the exclusive lease with a fail-closed deadline and durably fences every stale invocation before reading or removing a spool
v0.3 shared-worker and exclusive-recovery lease acquisition has a 900-second fail-closed timeout

v0.3 worker epoch metadata is portable and binds the immutable contract, invocation, window, and start time; the private runtime epoch additionally binds the local output identity and is removed with the work tree
v0.3 schedules eligible rows by primary source_host to rate_group-or-host lanes, preserves frozen order within lanes, and interleaves lanes in stable first-appearance round-robin order
v0.3 recovery-ledger tail damage is recorded in immutable JSON before truncation without recursively appending to the damaged ledger
v0.3 spool-recovery actions, artifact basenames, and row-identity presence use an exact fail-closed allowlist, including zero-byte prewrite removal
v0.3 wrapper requires the exact ordered nonempty scope base-check roster, allowing only the declared tail-recovery present-or-absent variant and failing closed on every other roster difference

v0.3 wrapper may adapt archive producer order to frozen base-verifier physical-source order only in a disposable private view after unique set equality, exact producer-order health rebuild, exact original contract, and equal sorted source/private-view content hashes
v0.3 terminal JSON and TSV receipt fields exclude local filesystem identities; private path-device-inode identity disappears with the work tree
a crash before evaluation and fsync is an unavoidable unreceipted boundary
pointer-health.tsv and strict rates use completion-covered attempts only
best-attempt selection orders first by identity priority and then by numeric attempt_index, never by second-resolution timestamp
abandoned attempts remain in physical attempt totals but never affect health
tail recovery records hash and length but never retains the raw discarded fragment
recognized orphan atomic-write temporary files are hash-and-length receipted before removal; unrecognized temporary names fail closed
pHash classes are diagnostic and never become recovery success
byte_exact skips decode and pHash
empty_response is retryable
each counted finality window must have a completion whose two-tier route-attempt protocol is complete
route status precedence is safety first, then direct policy or local blockers, then resolver outcome; a later resolver result cannot mask an earlier blocker
only committed direct_image and fallback_image attempts from protocol-complete windows can contribute finality observations
policy pending, local bandwidth deferral, oversize local response cap, and safety review do not contribute finality observations
any physical attempt safety_block, including an abandoned attempt, or any robots safety_block forces summary status FAIL
component-specific image and resolver/robots host maps constrain every request and redirect
credential-like query keys fail closed before network access and receipt URLs redact their values
rate-group byte caps include persistent in-flight reservations made before each response-body read
live audit and summarize receipts require and bind CPython 3.10.x
summary host_rate_policy and transient_backoff exactly equal the immutable audit contract
attempt_aggregations derive from all physical attempts, including abandoned attempts
response pixels are never retained in canonical ledgers, v0.3 private spools, or inter-process messages
v0.3 request starts share a flock-protected rate-state v3 and robots cache fills are per-invocation cross-process singleflight

completionRecord.description: Cross-field invariants: attempt_count equals the inclusive attempt range; fallback_attempt_count is no greater than resolver_candidate_count; resolution_protocol_complete is true exactly for a complete route-attempt status. completion_id binds the range and all four route-protocol fields.

tailRecoveryRecord.description: Cross-field invariant: original_size_bytes equals retained_size_bytes plus discarded_fragment_bytes. The raw discarded fragment is not retained.

parallelSpoolRecoveryRecord.description: Hash-bound v0.3 private-spool recovery evidence. artifact_name is basename-only and restricted to the three spool TSV names, invocation-work.json, or one of four recognized .target.<safe>.tmp forms; action and row-identity pairing are verified fail-closed. TSV tail removal requires original=retained+discarded and discarded>0; discard_empty_tsv_prewrite requires all sizes zero; incomplete attempt or robots tails require safety review. Complete JSON temporaries are promoted or deduplicated, incomplete JSON temporaries are quarantined by deletion after hash receipt, and no raw fragment is retained.

parallelRecoveryLedgerTailReceipt.description: Immutable non-recursive receipt fsynced before truncating a partial final row from parallel-spool-recoveries.tsv. recovery_id binds ledger name, size closure, and fragment hash; original_size_bytes equals retained_size_bytes plus discarded_fragment_bytes, a complete TSV header remains, and raw fragment bytes are not retained.

atomicTempRecoveryRecord.description: A recognized orphan from an interrupted atomic rewrite. recovery_id binds temporary_name, target_name, size_bytes, and SHA-256; the temporary bytes are removed only after this row is fsync-appended. Unknown temporary-name shapes fail closed.

hostRatePolicy.description: When rate_group is present, both max_bytes_per_hour and max_bytes_per_day are required and the group interval is shared across member hosts.

parallel_max_inflight.description: Required by the contract-v2 wrapper; absent from frozen serial v0.2 metadata.

parallel_worker_epoch.description: Portable contract/invocation/window/start binding required by the contract-v2 wrapper; absent from frozen serial v0.2 metadata.
